title: Myths of timing to correct
objectives: Correct five timing myths with the reality behind each.
Explain why “cash is safe while I wait” is wrong.
body_md:
“Experts know when the market will fall.” Reality: consistently timing both exit and re-entry is extremely rare. “Investing at a peak means I'll lose money.” Reality: over long horizons, the entry point usually matters far less than staying invested. “Stopping my SIP protects me in a fall.” Reality: it stops you buying units at lower prices. “I'll come back when things are clear.” Reality: when things look clear, prices have usually already recovered. “Cash is safe while I wait.” Reality: cash loses to inflation and misses rebounds.

| Myth | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "Experts know when the market will fall." | Consistently timing both exit and re-entry is extremely rare. |
| "Investing at a peak means I'll lose money." | Over long horizons, the entry point usually matters far less than staying invested. |
| "Stopping my SIP protects me in a fall." | It stops you buying units at lower prices. |
| "I'll come back when things are clear." | When things look clear, prices have usually already recovered. |
| "Cash is safe while I wait." | Cash loses to inflation and misses rebounds. |

> **Investor takeaway:** In a diversified, suitable fund, a market fall usually becomes a permanent loss only when you sell.
example: “I'll come back when things are clear”: by then, prices have usually already recovered — clarity arrives after the rebound.
say: Consistently timing both exit and re-entry is extremely rare.
Cash loses to inflation and misses rebounds.
never: Experts can time exits and re-entries reliably.
Stopping a SIP protects you in a fall.

check.q: Which line best sums up this module?
o: Time in the market matters more than timing the market
Exit when the market looks expensive
check.why: Time in the market matters more than timing the market. No one can reliably pick the best day; staying invested for the goal matters more.
